body.query: query { users { id name email created_at last_activity enabled is_guest } }

request.readOnlyPostReason: monday.com exposes data only through GraphQL, which uses POST for read queries. The query is read-only and changes nothing.

evidence.quote: passing the token in the `Authorization` header
Returns an array containing metadata about one or multiple users

assumptions: The docs do not say which API version is used when none is requested. The manifest uses older user fields (enabled, is_guest), which are marked for removal in version 2026-10. If the account's default version no longer has them, the query needs to move to status and kind.

The default query returns active and pending users only. The docs show that inactive (deactivated) users need a separate query (non_active: true, or status in version 2026-07+). Deactivated users who still hold licences are therefore probably missing.

The docs describe a page argument (starting at 1) and a limit argument, but a GraphQL page number can't be sent as a URL parameter. So no pagination is configured. From version 2026-07, a query with no limit returns at most 200 users, so larger accounts could be cut off.
The personal API token belongs to one person and stops working if that person leaves or the token is regenerated. Access also follows that person's permissions, so use an admin's token.
monday.com supports OAuth, but the token URL is not in the provided text, so OAuth is not listed.
Rate limit headers (RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy) are mentioned but their format isn't given, so they are left empty. The 5,000 requests per minute figure comes from the error table.
Errors arrive in an errors array, often with HTTP 200, but there is no simple success flag, so no error envelope is set.
last_activity is documented as a date with a zero time (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00), so activity is accurate to the day only.
The API base host is taken from the docs' code samples (https://api.monday.com/v2). The users field mapping is inferred from the documented field list.
